newsitem.title: BELGIUM: W.European airlines post 9.9 pct June traffic rise.
newsitem.headline: W.European airlines post 9.9 pct June traffic rise.

text.p: Major west European airlines posted a 9.9 percent year-on-year rise in passenger traffic for June, continuing a trend of strong demand, the Association of European Airlines (AEA) said on Thursday.
"The growth was evenly spread throughout the global route network," AEA, whose 26 member airlines include the region's main flag carriers, said in a statement.

Traffic on European services was up 9.4 percent, while on the busiest long-haul routes, across the North Atlantic and to the Far East and Australia, the increases were 10 and 10.2 percent respectively.
As capacity increased only six percent, the load factor improved by 2.6 percentage points to 75.5 percent, which AEA said was the highest-ever figure for the month of June.
AEA said this was a "remarkable result", noting that the two busiest months of summer were still to come.

"Load factors of this magnitude are good news for the airlines, since each additional passenger on an aeroplae does not incure an equivalent increase in fuel consumption and other operating costs," said AEA secretary-general Karl-Heinz Neumeister.
In the January-June period, passenger traffic rose 10.4 percent compared with the same period in 1996.
International freight carried by AEA members also grew over the period, rising 4.4 percent year-on-year in June and 3.5 percent in the first six months of the year compared with the same 1996 period.
